title: Privacy Governance Framework (PGF): Framework Overview and Component Guide
description:
The Privacy Governance Framework (PGF) is an operational framework for enterprise privacy governance. It connects a four-level architecture, 31 template-and-worked-example components and 23 processes to accountable business decisions.

This version provides a 32-page master overview and a complete editable English Markdown supplement, including the risk methodology, DPIA/TIA procedures, policies, registers, process ownership, assurance and reporting, a glossary, a conceptual standards crosswalk and a curated primary-source catalogue.

The integrated risk indicator maps directly to a configured likelihood band and matrix result; individual observations and DPO dissent accompany the authorised business decision without automatic per-metric tier overrides. Legal requirements and adopted release conditions remain separately visible. Templates are tool-neutral; the fictional bank's worked implementation names PAMOLA and clearly labels its deployment and numerical evidence as illustrative.

The GDPR is the baseline, with Canadian adaptation guidance and selected UK/Swiss transfer interfaces. Mappings to NIST, ENISA and Canadian accountability guidance are conceptual, not certification claims. No external peer review, empirical calibration, product capability certification or compliance guarantee is asserted.

Authors: Alexey Neyman and Val Khvatov. Rights holder: REALM INVEO. Original framework documentation/templates are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Software utilities, advanced companions and private/raw legacy records are excluded from this deposit.

Source edition: 28 October 2026. First public release: 29 October 2026. Regulatory reference snapshot: 26 October 2026.

Editable source repository: GitHub. Publication source snapshot: PGF 1.0.0.
